Marissa / Elena —

Quick note from outside counsel: Tectonica's commercial team will accept a split governing-law approach but insists that the injunctive relief carve explicitly permits Tectonica to obtain temporary equitable relief in NY state or federal court without first exhausting arbitration, limited to the preservation of trade secrets, access suspension for data exfiltration, and urgent escrow/escrowed-keys transfer.

We propose the following (high-level) carve: 
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, either party may seek temporary injunctive relief or any provisional remedy in the state or federal courts located in the State of New York to preserve intellectual property, prevent unauthorized access to customer data, or preserve escrowed materials; such relief shall not constitute a waiver of the obligation to arbitrate other disputes."

This keeps arbitration intact for the merits while allowing emergency relief. Happy to take direction from your counsel on narrowing the scope.

Team —

I reviewed Daniel's suggested carve and have a couple of edits to keep terms predictable and limit forum shopping: 

1) Narrow the triggers to three concrete categories (IP, data security incidents where exfiltration is reasonably suspected, and court-ordered preservation of escrow). Avoid vague "unauthorized access."

2) Add a 7-day notice/meet-and-confer requirement where practicable before filing in court, except where notice would defeat the purpose (e.g., active data exfiltration). This gives us a chance to escalate internally and offer temporary mitigations.

3) For governing law split: accept NY for order forms but require that any court filing invoking the injunctive carve be limited to venues in NY and that the MSA's substantive law remains California for interpretation of the Agreement (so statutory differences don't cascade).

Proposed language (short form):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Arbitration), either party may seek emergency provisional remedies in the state or federal courts sitting in New York to preserve intellectual property, address confirmed or reasonably suspected data exfiltration, or preserve escrowed materials. Except where notice would defeat the remedy, the seeking party shall provide at least seven (7) days’ written notice and an opportunity to meet-and-confer. Seeking such provisional relief shall not waive any right to arbitration of the underlying dispute. For clarity, the choice of governing law in the Master Services Agreement shall remain the laws of the State of California."

Ben / Marissa — if you approve, I'll add this as a redline to our draft and send back to Tectonica's counsel with a short comment explaining the notice exception. We should also flag for Sales that a split-law approach requires our order-form template to carry a jurisdiction clause mapping to the commercial terms.
